worksheet.title: Put It in Order
worksheet.subtitle: Four steps in the right order
worksheet.learning_goal: I can put four steps in order from first to last.

parts.title: Bit's plant grows step by step
parts.text: Bit's plant grows a new leaf each day: 1 leaf, then 2, then 3, then 4. The steps go in order from fewest to most.

parts.title: Write the order
parts.prompt: Write 1, 2, 3, 4 under the mixed-up steps to put them in order (fewest leaves to most).

parts.title: Which is first? Which is last?
parts.prompt: Circle the step that is FIRST (1 leaf). Put an X on the step that is LAST (4 leaves).

parts.title: You try — draw the next step
parts.prompt: After 4 leaves comes day 5. Draw the next step (5 leaves).

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Putting several steps in the right order makes a plan. A plan of ordered steps is an algorithm — and computers follow them step by step.

teacher_guide.title: Put It in Order
teacher_guide.subtitle: Quick facilitation notes & answer key
teacher_guide.footer_topic: 3. Put It in Order — Teacher Guide

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Children sequence four steps into the correct order (fewest to most). Arranging several steps in order is the heart of building an algorithm — a plan a computer can follow step by step.

parts.title: Kindergarten frame (Ontario)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children order a multi-step process.
No reading required of the child: read each prompt aloud; the child writes 1-4 and draws.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet + a pencil. Optional: cards with 1-4 dots to lay out in order by hand.

parts.title: Run it (about 15 min)
text: 1. MODEL: count the in-order plant — 'one leaf, two, three, four.' The count grows by one each day.
2. GUIDED: Exercise 1 — number the mixed cards by counting leaves (fewest = 1).
3. YOU TRY: children mark first and last (Ex 2), then draw day 5 with five leaves (Ex 3).
4. Connect: 'A plan of ordered steps is an algorithm — computers follow them in order.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Model — in order: 1 leaf, 2 leaves, 3 leaves, 4 leaves.
Ex 1 — under the mixed cards [4, 2, 1, 3 leaves] write [4, 2, 1, 3].
Ex 2 — circle the 1-leaf card (first); X on the 4-leaf card (last).
Ex 3 — draw a step with 5 leaves (▲ ▲ ▲ ▲ ▲).

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: numbering left-to-right by position — have them count leaves before writing.
Simplify: order three cards (1-3) before four.
Extend: shuffle and re-order, or order steps of a real routine (wash, dry, etc.).
Movement option: hand four children 1-4 objects and have them line up in order.

parts.title: Success looks like
parts.text: The child numbers the four steps 1-4 by count and draws a correct five-leaf next step.
